Description: An introductory course covering the foundations of law, legal systems, and the structure of the Zambian judiciary. Students are introduced to legal reasoning, interpretation of statutes, and the role of law in society.
LearningOutcomes: Understand the structure and function of the Zambian legal system
Identify and apply key sources of law including statutes and case law
Demonstrate basic legal reasoning and statutory interpretation skills

Description: A detailed examination of the Constitution of Zambia, including fundamental rights, the separation of powers, and constitutional interpretation. Students analyse landmark constitutional cases and their implications for governance.
LearningOutcomes: Analyse the structure and provisions of the Constitution of Zambia
Evaluate the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms under constitutional law
Apply constitutional principles to practical governance and legal scenarios

Description: This course examines the legal framework governing commercial transactions and corporate entities in Zambia. Topics include contract formation, company incorporation, directors' duties, and commercial dispute resolution.
LearningOutcomes: Explain the legal requirements for forming and managing companies under Zambian law
Analyse commercial contracts and identify legal obligations and remedies
Apply principles of company law to resolve corporate governance disputes

Description: An introduction to micro and macroeconomic principles, including supply and demand, market structures, national income, inflation, and economic policy. Students gain a foundational understanding of how economies function.
LearningOutcomes: Explain core microeconomic and macroeconomic concepts and their interrelationships
Analyse the impact of economic policies on business and consumer behaviour
Apply economic reasoning to evaluate real-world market scenarios

Description: A comprehensive study of financial accounting principles and practices, including the preparation and analysis of financial statements in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). Students develop practical bookkeeping and reporting skills.
LearningOutcomes: Prepare accurate financial statements including income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements
Apply IFRS standards to record and report business transactions
Analyse financial data to assess organisational performance and financial health

Description: An exploration of individual, group, and organisational dynamics that influence workplace behaviour. Topics include motivation, leadership, team dynamics, organisational culture, and change management.
LearningOutcomes: Analyse theories of motivation and their application in organisational settings
Evaluate leadership styles and their effects on team performance
Develop strategies to manage organisational change and improve workplace culture

Description: An introductory survey of the health sciences field, covering the structure of healthcare systems, public health principles, and the determinants of health. Students explore the Zambian healthcare landscape and global health challenges.
LearningOutcomes: Describe the structure and function of the Zambian national healthcare system
Identify key social, economic, and environmental determinants of health
Explain the roles of various health professionals within multidisciplinary care teams

Description: A systematic study of the human body's structural organisation and physiological processes. Topics include the musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, respiratory, and nervous systems, with emphasis on clinical relevance to health sciences practice.
LearningOutcomes: Identify and describe major anatomical structures and organ systems of the human body
Explain key physiological processes and homeostatic mechanisms
Relate anatomical and physiological knowledge to health conditions encountered in clinical practice

Description: An examination of the principles of epidemiology and public health practice in the context of sub-Saharan Africa. Students study disease surveillance, outbreak investigation, health promotion, and the epidemiology of communicable diseases such as malaria, HIV/AIDS, and tuberculosis in Zambia.
LearningOutcomes: Apply epidemiological methods to investigate disease patterns and outbreaks
Evaluate public health interventions and their effectiveness in the Zambian context
Analyse data to identify risk factors and inform evidence-based health policy
